annotation_description: Failed to play a land before casting Winternight Stories. Playing a Swamp first would leave 4 lands available after resolution (1 untapped), which could matter after drawing 3 new cards - for instance if they draw a 1-mana spell like Bloodthorn Flail or another Insatiable Avarice.

message: Select card to discard (selected 0 of 2, min 2)
annotation_description: Winternight Stories allows discarding just one creature card instead of two non-creature cards. Discarding two Swamps (net +1 card) instead of one Harvester of Misery (net +2 cards) costs an extra card. While Harvester is powerful, with 3 lands on board plus Restless Reef, Gloomlake Verge, and Watery Grave still in hand, the second Swamp is nearly worthless - making the effective cost of keeping Harvester very low.

Opus Valley targeted Greasewrench Goblin with Bitter Triumph instead of Marauding Mako. The Goblin's exhaust ability was already used (evidenced by the +1/+1 counter), making it just a 3/2 body. Marauding Mako grows with every discard trigger, and o3 Tinker is running a discard-synergy deck with Bloodthorn Flail in hand, Inti in graveyard (recurring discard value), and the overall deck strategy centered on discarding cards. The Mako would become a much larger threat over time.

Missed lethal. Could have discarded Flamewake Phoenix to equip Bloodthorn Flail onto Bloodghast (equip cost: discard a card), triggering Monument to Endurance for 'each opponent loses 3 life' (opponent goes from 6 to 3), then attacked with a 4/2 Bloodghast for exactly lethal (3 + 4 = 7 > 6).

Exiling Winternight Stories (which has Harmonize - castable from graveyard) and Archenemy's Charm (a powerful removal/recursion spell) for evidence when there are clearly expendable cards available. Stock Up (3) + Bitter Triumph (2) + Intimidation Tactics (1) = 6 MV exactly, all with no graveyard utility.

message: Choose mode (selected 0 of 2147483647, min 1): Insatiable Avarice
chosen_display: 1. Search your library for a card, then shuffle and put that card on top.
annotation_description: Opus Valley is at 2 life and chose only the tutor mode of Insatiable Avarice (pay {2} to search), which just puts a card on top of their library. They need an answer RIGHT NOW to survive - Flamewake Phoenix is already attacking them. By not also choosing the draw-3 mode (+{B}{B} to draw three cards and lose 3 life), they could have... wait, they're at 2 life, so paying 3 life would kill them. The tutor-only mode means they won't draw the card until next turn's draw step, and they need to survive this turn. However, given they're at 2 life, the draw mode would be suicide (lose 3 life at 2 HP). So the tutor mode is actually the only viable choice. But the real question is whether casting Insatiable Avarice at all is correct here - they have all lands tapped and 3 Requiting Hex in hand. Looking more carefully: all their lands are tapped, so they already cast the Insatiable Avarice. The tutor-only mode is the only one that doesn't kill them. This seems reasonable given the constraints.
